nagatitan:study:1.title: The first sauropod dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous Khok Kruat Formation of Thailand enriches the diversity of somphospondylan titanosauriforms in southeast Asia (Scientific Reports, 2026)

facts.statement: The Nagatitan fossil material was discovered in 2016 by Thanom Luangnan in Chaiyaphum province, Thailand.
facts.quote: The Nagatitan fossil material was discovered in outcrops of the Khok Kruat Formation in Chaiyaphum province, Thailand by Thanom Luangnan on the bank of a pond in 2016.

facts.statement: The overall body length was calculated to be about 27.2 meters.
facts.quote: The overall body length was calculated at about 27.2 m.

facts.statement: Nagatitan is classified as a euhelopodid macronarian sauropod.
Phylogenetic analysis recovered Nagatitan within the family Euhelopodidae.
facts.quote: Nagatitan was recovered within the somphospondylan titanosauriform family Euhelopodidae.

facts.statement: Under equal character weighting, Nagatitan was placed as the sister taxon to the European genus Europatitan at the base of Euhelopodidae.
facts.quote: Using equal weighting, it was placed as the sister taxon to Europatitan—a European taxon not generally regarded as a member of this otherwise Asian clade—at the base of Euhelopodidae.

facts.statement: Under implied weighting, Nagatitan was placed in a more derived position within Euhelopodidae, diverging after Tangvayosaurus but before Phuwiangosaurus.
facts.quote: Using implied weighting, Europatitan shifted outside of this clade, while Nagatitan was placed in a more euhelopodid derived position, diverging after Tangvayosaurus but before Phuwiangosaurus.

facts.statement: Nagatitan lived during the Early Cretaceous, specifically the Aptian to Albian ages.
Nagatitan lived between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Albian (121.4 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Nagatitan is known from the Khok Kruat Formation in Thailand.
facts.quote: Nagatitan () is an extinct genus of euhelopodid sauropod dinosaur known from the Early Cretaceous (Aptian–Albian ages) Khok Kruat Formation of Thailand.
